name: Phase-free state copy
summary: A phase-free X-state (|0⟩) copies through a phase-free Z-spider.
description:
A phase-free X-spider with a single leg is, up to a scalar, the computational basis state $|0\rangle$. When it is plugged into a phase-free Z-spider, the Z-spider copies it to all of its other legs.

This is the form in which state copying appears as an axiom in most completeness results; it is the case $a = 0$, $\alpha = 0$ of the general [state copy](../state-copy/) rule, which copies both basis states through a Z-spider with any phase. Many papers write the scalar $\sqrt2^{-(n-1)}$ as a diagram.
parameter_notes: n is the number of output legs of the Z-spider (shown for n = 2).
